newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end down and on support, trade brisk.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end down and on support, trade brisk.

text.p: FCOJ September futures closed barely firmer but remained below key 76.00 cents.
September settled up 0.05 cent at 75.88 cents a lb, having ranged from 76.15 to 75.10 cents. The rest of the board closed 0.15 cent higher to 0.40 cent weaker.
An estimated 4,000 lots changed hands on the day compared with Wednesday's official 3,973 lots.
While prices have failed to sustain gains and pierce the recent high of 78.25 cents basis September, the lows have also remained intact.
"We broke support (76.00 cents on Wednesday) but we couldn't do anything with it," PaineWebber analyst Bernard Savaiko, said.
"The market is making new lows without any downside follow-through. It's almost as if the market has lost its downside momentum.
Still, record crops forecast for Florida and Brazil will continue to weigh on the market.
Analysts expect prices to drift in a 78.00-75.00 cent trading range ahead of a private estimate of the 1997/98 Florida crop by Citrus Consulting International, on August 14.
The USDA will issue its estimate of the crop in October.
